subject: Request: Private Offer — unusual rev-share tiering + Net90 payment (Helix Systems)
messages:
From: Sam Riley <sam.riley@helixsystems.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Private offer ask — flexible rev-share tiers + Net90 payment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Helix is ready to move to a private offer on AWS but procurement has two constraints they say are non-negotiable for their global reseller program:

- Payment term: Net90 (grouped across EMEA/APAC)
- Rev-share: a sliding-tier that starts at 18% for initial 6 months and steps to 22% tied to committed monthly spend; they also want a carveout so co-marketing credits don’t count toward the committed spend.

We understand this is outside standard marketplace templates. We attached our latest MOA redlines and a small revenue model. Can Redwood consider a one-time exception for these terms? Helix is a strategic target for our product-led channel push and a multi-year commit is realistic if we can get this structure in place.

Sam Riley
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Helix Systems
Attachments: Helix_MOA_v3_redlines.pdf, revshare_model_helix.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private offer ask — flexible rev-share tiers + Net90 payment

Karthik / Ben / Laura — looping you in. Helix wants a non-standard private offer on AWS with two asks that require exec clearance: Net90 payment and a sliding rev-share tier that excludes co-marketing credits from committed spend.

Key points:
- ARR upside: Helix expects to onboard 10 enterprise customers via their reseller program in first year; model attached shows ~1.2M ARR in year one.
- Risk: Net90 increases collection exposure and our Marketplace payout timing; rev-share carveout lowers our effective take rate if credits are large.
- Request: one-time executive exception with clear guardrails (timebox the tiering to 12 months, set a minimum committed spend threshold, and require a co-sell milestone).

Please review the attached MOA redlines and revenue model. I recommend we escalate to Evelyn for final sign-off if finance/legal are comfortable. Ben, quick note on commercial rationale?

Thanks — Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 14:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer ask — flexible rev-share tiers + Net90 payment

Marissa,

Quick read-through and initial thoughts:

- Rev-share sliding tiers: acceptable if we protect a guaranteed floor (e.g., 15% floor) and limit the window to 12 months. Also recommend including a clawback if Helix fails to achieve the committed spend within 90 days of each tiering milestone.
- Co-marketing carveout: carveouts are common but need definition — propose we explicitly exclude only third-party marketing credits, not discounts applied to customer invoices.
- Net90: this is my main concern. Marketplace payouts and revenue recognition get messy. If we must accept Net90, require: (a) a one-time holdback equal to 10% of first two months' payout until funds received, or (b) require Helix to pre-fund Marketplace fees into an escrow with AWS. Either option reduces our receivable exposure.

I can draft the term language and a short risk memo. If finance signs off on the holdback/escrow approach I think this is a defensible exception.

Karthik
Deal Desk
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer ask — flexible rev-share tiers + Net90 payment

Team — finance view:

- Net90 increases DSO materially vs our standard Net30/Marketplace cadence. I don’t love it but will consider for strategic accounts if controls exist.
- Recommended controls: 1) 10% holdback on payouts until payment clears for first 90 days; 2) require Helix to sign an ACH mandate and provide a primary and backup payment method; 3) require explicit language that refunds/credits reduce the committed spend calculation.

If we can push the holdback and ACH mandate into the MOA, I can sign off and we can present the package to Evelyn for exec approval.

Laura
VP, Finance
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec ask: Helix private offer exception — asking for one-time approval

Evelyn — short ask for your sign-off. Helix is a channel-first partner that will introduce Redwood via AWS Marketplace to ~15 enterprise prospects over 12 months. Key commercial trade-offs we propose in exchange for the exception:

- Timebound rev-share tiering (12 months) with a 15% guaranteed floor and clawback triggers;
- Explicit carveout language for third-party co-marketing credits only (no invoice discounts);
- 10% holdback on early payouts tied to payment receipt;
- Minimum committed spend: $300k ARR in first 12 months or exception expires.

This is a one-off structure and Ben commits contractually to drive the committed spend velocity and a co-sell plan with Helix. If approved, legal will finalize MOA language and finance will operationalize the holdback.

I recommend approval with the listed guardrails.

—Ben
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 21:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec ask: Helix private offer exception — asking for one-time approval

Thanks all — I approve the exception on the conditions Ben outlined. Mandatory items before signature:

1) Legal to produce MOA with explicit clawback and definition of co-marketing credits;
2) Finance to implement 10% holdback for first 90 days and confirm how Marketplace payout ops will be executed;
3) Sales to commit to a minimum $300k ARR and provide a 90-day cadence update to me;
4) This approval is for AWS private offer only and is valid for this Helix MOA; any replication requires separate approval.

Marissa — please coordinate legal/ops and get the redlined MOA back in my inbox for final signature.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue Operations
